details:
ARES EVA Planner – Marswalk Planner

ARES EVA Planner is an interactive web application designed to support the planning of Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) on Mars, specifically in Jezero Crater. It allows users to create exploration routes by selecting points of interest directly on the map, adjusting waypoints, and analyzing mission parameters in real time.

How it works: The application calculates route distance, estimated walking time, elevation changes, oxygen consumption, return time, and potential hazards. It also includes a scientific value assessment based on nearby geological targets, a resource exploration section, and tools to review, print, and export mission plans in GeoJSON format.

Benefits and expected impact: The project aims to improve the conceptual planning of future human exploration missions to Mars. By combining route planning, resource identification, and safety considerations, it helps users understand the challenges astronauts may face and how mission efficiency could be improved.

Tools and technologies: We developed the application using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. We integrated NASA Mars Trek geographic references and NASA ArcGIS REST services to access Martian geological information. We also used GitHub and GitHub Pages to manage and publish the application. No specialized hardware was required.

Creativity and innovation: Our main innovation is bringing scientific exploration, astronaut mobility, and survival-related planning together in one interactive platform. Instead of simply displaying a map of Mars, we transformed it into a mission-planning environment.

Team considerations: During development, we considered astronaut safety, limited oxygen supplies, walking time, terrain conditions, return-to-habitat distance, scientific relevance, resource availability, data reliability, and user experience. We also considered the limitations of available planetary data and the importance of making our calculations and assumptions understandable.
